newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates seen rising sharply at auction.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates seen rising sharply at auction.

text.p: Nervousness over the upcoming elections in Mexico could push the yield on the bellwether 28-day Cetes up by as much as 300 basis points at the primary auction on Tuesday, analysts said on Monday.
The expectations of the strong rate hike were fueled after Banco de Mexico assigned a one-day 715 million peso credit in the secondary market for 24.72 percent on Monday.
"Banco de Mexico has signaled with the higher rates that we think there could be a rebound in primary rates," said Casa de Bolsa Value analyst, Martin Delgado.
Mexicans will vote for a new lower house in Congress, as well as part of the Senate, governors in six states and the mayor of Mexico City on July 6.
MMS International said it expects rates to rise in the short end of the curve but to remain stable in the long run.
The 28-day paper was assigned last week at 20.90 percent.
Mexican treasury bill rates are also seen being affected by some uncertainty over U.S. interest rates ahead of the Open Market Committee Meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve this week.
Analysts said, however, that any increase in rates will likely be short-term and rates could restart their downward trend after the elections.
"All the economic indicators are positive enough, and definitely the macro position is better for lower interest rates, rather than higher rates," said Mexico City economist Jonathan Heath.
He said that the nervousness expected before the elections was less than originally expected.
